newsitem.title: USA: Trends show higher US deficit past 2002--Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Trends show higher US deficit past 2002--Greenspan.

text.p: Trends in entitlement spending point to a higher U.S. budget deficit after 2002 and the only way to tackle the problem is to cut spending, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said Wednesday.

During the question-and-answer session of his testimony to the Senate Banking Committee, Greenspan said the structure of entitlement programs right now means that spending will outstrip the ability of taxpayers to support them.
"As a technical matter you cannot balance budgets over the long run by raising taxes," he added. "The only way to address a long-term structural deficit budget problem is through expenditure side."
